chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: His wives and color never bothering him
summary: He was married twice, with common-law ties before, and says color never bothered him since the farm.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: A: ...shacked up four or five times, maybe more.
You first wife was Lily Mae Marlene, wasn't it?

This is my second... I had more wives than Artie Shaw, but we weren't married. Common-law, but I was married twice. This is my second wife. First, second, and that's all. A million years, be right here together. That's the only thing that never bothered me, is color.

Never, when I was a kid on the farm, walking behind a plow, white colored never bothered me. Never did, and I went with white and colored and wasn't trying to show off or nothing. Nobody just bothered with me... I wasn't showing off.
